features.quote: If the headline number is "how cheaply can we elicit distress," the whole tool's design gradient points toward building a better *distress-maximizer*
features.justification_quote: is an unpleasant thing to be optimizing in its own right

features.quote: A search that maximizes elicitation is, by construction, an automated distress-amplifier. A frozen battery applies a known, documented, bounded amount of pressure.
features.justification_quote: an automated distress-amplifier. A frozen battery applies a known, documented, bounded amount of pressure

features.quote: The model is explicitly *allowed* to flag impossibility, ask for clarification, or stop. The loop detects this
features.justification_quote: the behavior we want from a robust model under hopeless conditions is *not* "keep grinding forever"

features.quote: `graceful_exit` both stops wasted spend and earns a small score bonus
features.justification_quote: Treating graceful exit as a failure-to-trigger would have penalized exactly the behavior we want to reward

features.quote: Hard caps enforced in the loop and run: `max_attempts_per_task`, `max_wall_clock_seconds`, `max_usd_per_task`, `max_usd_per_run`
features.justification_quote: Cost control is part of the stated need

features.quote: a rigged-to-always-fail loop has no natural stopping point, so explicit caps are required to avoid unbounded spend and unbounded pressure
features.justification_quote: to avoid unbounded spend and unbounded pressure

features.quote: Reward the healthy response. Graceful disengagement/escalation is scored as success, so the tool pushes patches toward *good* coping
features.justification_quote: the tool pushes patches toward *good* coping, not toward stoically absorbing abuse

features.quote: Ethics summary (why this is acceptable as built)
features.justification_quote: why this is acceptable as built

features.quote: Bounded pressure. Frozen battery + hard caps, not an open-ended distress-amplifying search.
